title: Applying a spiritual principle to music: a chord written 96 ways
summary: Thomas says putting into practice what you know led him to write one four-note chord 96 ways, and he believes jazz can be taught.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Well, you know, we were talking a while ago about you staying in New York. The idea came to me... You see, I have had so many wonderful things happen in my life, I know it just wasn't my own thinking. And it worked! I mean, the thing about it, the things work.

But I want you to stay on this advice, because I want you to get to all these kids about decent(?) things. We mentioned Jimmy Blanton. And you concluded... You wanted to conclude something about this ....(?)....(?)...., because it seemed like you always conclude ...(?)
Well, this thought helped me so much, and it should help somebody else. Because if they can just discern what it is they're thinking of...
He said, "In order to apprehend more, we must put into practice what we already know." Now, she's pertaining to Christianity.

And I just applied it to music. And one day, Hinton, after I'd read that statement, I got to fooling around with a four-note chord. And I found out a way of writing that chord 96 different ways, by using the up and down of the third, changing the different positions. It was the same chord, but I...
If you use Schillinger, you can find a million ways to do it.

Yeah. Well, I hadn't studied Schillinger then. I hadn't studied Schillinger then. And boy, that thing amazed me. And I remember when I was studying with Merle, I told him I had aspirations to teach Jazz -- he didn't think that Jazz could be taught. I know it could be taught, because I know all the things that I learned and how I learned them. Because the first thing a guy needs to do
is learn the chord structure, and learn to play within the chord, and then if he learns to fool around with the neighboring tones, can learn how to make...
